goal: Trace each actual outside incidence of a cubic assigned first neighbour through its component of G minus the one handoff envelope support, proving the second attachment forced by bridgelessness and retaining its possible landing sites.
objects: G = selected.object and the complete window-history post-[144] ExactLedger
one source pattern and its one decorated envelope inside the same typeBHandoff witness
the vertex support S of that envelope, its assigned first neighbours K_h and arms, and components C of G-S
interaction: An actual edge from an assigned cubic first neighbour into a component C of G-S is a boundary edge of a genuine G cut; bridgelessness requires a second edge across that cut, whose landing in S may or may not be another assigned neighbour.
acceptance: For each actual outside incidence, identify its component C, show that its G-boundary has at least two distinct edges using bridgelessness, and classify the same-first-neighbour landing exception by positive versus zero arm length. Do not claim that every neighbour has an outside edge, that the second attachment reaches another K_h or source pair, or that a forbidden cycle, cap, or closure follows.
on_failure: If no outside incidence exists, preserve that live case. If the second boundary edge lands at an unassigned vertex or another support coordinate, record it rather than changing the envelope or source-pattern assignment.
